title: Ziekmelding: nature-of-illness (AVG art.9) verplicht ingevoerd én automatisch gedeeld met inlener
evidence:
CONFIRMED in three paths.

1) Collection — health data made REQUIRED:
- src/pages/portal/PortalSickReport.tsx:125 Label "Reden / klachten"; :129 placeholder "Beschrijf je klachten..." (solicits nature of illness = AVG art.9 special-category data).
- PortalSickReport.tsx:68 `if (!reason.trim()) throw new Error('Vul een reden in')` and :144 button disabled `!reason.trim()` — the complaint is REQUIRED to submit.
- PortalSickReport.tsx:78 stores it in `sick_reports.notes`.

2) Auto-forwarding of the complaint to the inlener (no consent, no review):
- supabase/functions/_shared/sick-report-handler.ts:288-291 renders `data.notes` into the client email under "Toelichting".
- sick-report-handler.ts:181-199 builds that HTML and sends via `sendViaOutlookAccount` to the inlener contact (`contact.email`).
- sick-report-handler.ts:215 also copies the complaint into `communications.body`.
- Trigger path: process-sick-report/index.ts:57 → cascadeSickReport runs the email automatically right after portal submit (PortalSickReport.tsx:87-89 invokes 'process-sick-report').

3) WhatsApp path stores the raw complaint and auto-forwards it:
- supabase/functions/whatsapp-webhook/index.ts:418 inserts the free-text reason verbatim into `notes`.
- whatsapp-webhook/index.ts:426 calls cascadeSickReport → same inlener email containing `notes`.

Schema: sick_reports has only `notes` (text) as the free-text field (src/integrations/supabase/types.ts:7517-7531); no separation between operational note and medical reason, and no consent flag. No existing migration mitigates this (grep for nature_of_illness/art9/client_visible returns nothing in supabase/migrations).
rootCause: The single free-text `sick_reports.notes` field conflates an operational/administrative note with the medical "nature of illness" (AVG art.9 bijzondere persoonsgegevens). The portal makes that medical reason mandatory, and the cascade pipeline (both portal and WhatsApp) unconditionally injects `notes` into the email that is auto-sent to the inlener (opdrachtgever). Under AVG/GDPR an uitzendbureau may register that a worker is sick, but the nature/aard of the illness must not be required nor disclosed to the inlener (inlener only needs absence + expected return). There is no consent step, no recruiter review gate, and no field-level separation.
fixSummary: Separate the medical reason from the operational notification and never auto-share the nature-of-illness with the inlener. (1) Add an internal-only `reason_internal` column to sick_reports (RLS: is_internal_user/self only, never exposed to inlener email). (2) Make the portal reason OPTIONAL and clearly label it as internal-only, writing it to `reason_internal` (and a neutral operational note to `notes`). (3) Remove `notes`/medical reason from the inlener email body and from the communications log copy — the inlener email keeps only candidate name, function, reported date, and expected return. (4) WhatsApp path writes the captured reason to `reason_internal`, not `notes`. (5) Data-cleanup migration moves existing `notes` content into `reason_internal` and nulls `notes` so historical medical text is no longer in the inlener-facing field.
fixSteps: MIGRATION (new file supabase/migrations/20260615120000_sick_report_avg_art9_separation.sql): ADD COLUMN reason_internal text to public.sick_reports. Backfill: `UPDATE public.sick_reports SET reason_internal = notes WHERE notes IS NOT NULL AND reason_internal IS NULL;` then `UPDATE public.sick_reports SET notes = NULL WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;` (notes becomes a neutral operational field going forward; the medical reason now lives in reason_internal which is never put in the inlener email). Keep RLS unchanged — reason_internal inherits the existing tenant_select/tenant_update (is_internal_user) + the worker self policies on sick_reports, so the inlener (client portal / opdrachtgever role) never reads it via RLS, and crucially the cascade email no longer includes it.

sick-report-handler.ts: in cascadeSickReport SELECT (lines 76-80) add `reason_internal` to the selected columns ONLY if needed for the recruiter_task (it already builds the task from `report.notes`; switch the task description/priority logic at lines 138-143 to read `report.reason_internal ?? report.notes`). REMOVE `notes` from the inlener email: in buildClientEmailHtml call (lines 181-189) drop the `notes` argument, and delete the 'Toelichting' table row (lines 288-291) plus the `notes:` field on the data object (line 188) and its type (line 257). The inlener email then contains only candidateName, functionName, companyName, reportedAt, expectedReturnDate.

sick-report-handler.ts: at the communications insert (lines 208-219) change `body` (line 215) to a neutral string WITHOUT the medical reason, e.g. `body: \`Ziekmelding voor ${candidateName}\`` — do not append `report.notes`.

PortalSickReport.tsx: make the reason OPTIONAL and internal-only. Remove the hard require at line 68 (`if (!reason.trim()) throw...`) and the disabled gate at line 144 (`!reason.trim()`). Relabel line 125 from 'Reden / klachten' to e.g. 'Toelichting (optioneel, alleen voor je intercedent)' and change placeholder line 129 to a neutral hint like 'Optioneel — alleen voor intern gebruik'. In the insert (lines 71-83) write the free text to `reason_internal` instead of `notes` (set `notes: null` or a neutral operational note, and `reason_internal: reason.trim() || null`). Add a short helper text that the nature of illness is not shared with the opdrachtgever.

whatsapp-webhook/index.ts: in createSickReportFromWhatsApp (lines 413-422) move the captured reason out of the inlener-facing `notes`. Keep a neutral operational label in `notes` (e.g. `Automatisch uit WhatsApp (${deadlineLabel}, deadline ${automation.sick_report_deadline_time})`) and put the raw `reason.slice(0,500)` into a new `reason_internal` field instead. This keeps the deadline label (used by cascadeSickReport's 'na deadline' check at sick-report-handler.ts:138) working — but update that check to read reason_internal/notes consistently per step 2.

Regenerate types: run mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__generate_typescript_types after apply_migration and write to src/integrations/supabase/types.ts so `reason_internal` appears on sick_reports Row/Insert/Update (currently lines 7515-7560).

Verify: `deno check supabase/functions/process-sick-report/index.ts supabase/functions/whatsapp-webhook/index.ts supabase/functions/_shared/sick-report-handler.ts` and `npm run typecheck`. Manually confirm the rendered inlener email (send-match-proposal style preview or a unit assertion on buildClientEmailHtml output) no longer contains any 'Toelichting' / medical text.
migrationSql:
-- B1: AVG art.9 — scheid medische 'aard van de ziekte' van de operationele ziekmelding.
-- De aard van de ziekte mag NIET verplicht zijn en NIET met de inlener gedeeld worden.
-- We verplaatsen bestaande vrije-tekst klachten uit `notes` (die in de inlener-mail
-- belandde) naar een intern-only kolom `reason_internal`, en maken `notes` leeg.
-- reason_internal erft de bestaande RLS op sick_reports (tenant_* = is_internal_user()
-- + de _self_ policies van de medewerker); de opdrachtgever/client-portal leest het nooit,
-- en de cascade-mail bevat het niet meer (zie code-fix in sick-report-handler.ts).

BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE public.sick_reports
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reason_internal text;

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.sick_reports.reason_internal IS
  'AVG art.9: interne toelichting/aard van de ziekte. Alleen zichtbaar voor interne rollen en de medewerker zelf; NOOIT gedeeld met de inlener.';

-- Backfill: bestaande klachten naar de interne kolom.
UPDATE public.sick_reports
   SET reason_internal = notes
 WHERE notes IS NOT NULL
   AND reason_internal IS NULL;

-- Verwijder de medische tekst uit het (potentieel inlener-zichtbare) notes-veld.
-- `notes` blijft bestaan als neutraal operationeel veld voor toekomstige inserts.
UPDATE public.sick_reports
   SET notes = NULL
 WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.sick_reports.notes IS
  'Neutrale operationele notitie (geen medische aard van de ziekte). De aard van de ziekte staat in reason_internal.';

COMMIT;

newFiles.purpose: Add internal-only reason_internal column to sick_reports, backfill existing notes into it, and null out notes so the medical nature-of-illness is no longer stored in the inlener-facing field.

risk: Destructive + prod-touching: the cleanup migration NULLs existing sick_reports.notes after copying into reason_internal — if reason_internal already held other data the WHERE reason_internal IS NULL guard prevents overwrite, but the second UPDATE permanently clears notes (intended). De-risk: run on a Supabase branch first, snapshot/backup the table (`CREATE TABLE sick_reports_notes_backup_20260615 AS SELECT id, notes FROM sick_reports WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;`) before the NULL update, and require human confirmation before applying to prod. Functional risk: cascadeSickReport's 'na deadline' check (sick-report-handler.ts:138) reads notes — must be repointed to reason_internal/notes consistently or task priority logic breaks; covered in fixSteps. Behavioral change: inlener email no longer shows any toelichting (intended, GDPR-correct). Out of scope but noted: WhatsApp inserts omit employee_id while types.ts marks it NOT NULL — verify the live column is nullable/defaulted; not changed by this fix.

title: cv-rewrite leaks raw PII (name, email, phone, DOB, nationality) to Lovable third-party AI gateway without pseudonymization
evidence:
CONFIRMED in this code.

1) supabase/functions/cv-rewrite/index.ts:30-35 — selects raw PII from candidates: `id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, address_city, date_of_birth, nationality, skills, languages, certifications, ...`.

2) index.ts:67-78 — the `anonymous` branch masks ONLY first_name/last_name/email/phone/address_*. It does NOT mask `date_of_birth` or `nationality`. So even in "anonymous" mode, DOB + nationality (a special-category-adjacent attribute under AVG/GDPR art. 9-adjacent) leak.

3) index.ts:85-91 — the full candidate object is `JSON.stringify`'d straight into the userPrompt.

4) index.ts:93-99 — that prompt is POSTed to `https://ai.gateway.lovable.dev/v1/chat/completions` (a third-party gateway, distinct from the EU VPS / Anthropic paths). No pseudonymization anywhere.

5) src/pages/CvTool.tsx:27 — `anonymous` defaults to `false`, so the DEFAULT call ships full name + email + phone + DOB + nationality to Lovable.

6) Contrast: supabase/functions/analyze-cv/index.ts:12 imports `pseudonymizeCv`, and index.ts:277-281 applies it to all outbound dossier text before any provider call. cv-rewrite has NO such import (verified: grep for pseudonymize in cv-rewrite returns nothing).

7) src/pages/CvTool.tsx:130 — the candidate's real name is rendered CLIENT-SIDE from the local candidate object; the AI output is only section prose (summary/experience/skills/education/languages/certifications, per the tool schema at index.ts:111-123). So the gateway never needs identifiers/DOB/nationality to function — they can be stripped with zero loss of capability.
rootCause: cv-rewrite was written to pass the entire candidate row (incl. direct identifiers and DOB/nationality) verbatim to a third-party LLM gateway, treating the `anonymous` UI toggle as the only privacy control. That toggle (a) defaults to false and (b) is incomplete (never masks date_of_birth or nationality). Unlike analyze-cv, this function never adopted the mandatory `pseudonymizeCv` data-minimization step before outbound transfer, so personal data is exported to a third party for every default rewrite — an AVG art. 5 (data minimisation) / art. 44+ (third-country/third-party transfer) violation.
fixSummary: Stop sending direct identifiers and DOB/nationality to the Lovable gateway entirely (they are not needed — the CV section prose does not require them, and the real name is re-attached client-side). Build a minimized payload containing only non-identifying professional fields, drop date_of_birth and nationality unconditionally, always pseudonymize the placement history (which can contain names/companies as free text) and the serialized payload via the existing pseudonymizeCv helper as a defense-in-depth net, and remove the now-redundant partial `anonymous` masking. Single-file edit; no migration, no schema change, non-destructive, not prod-data-touching.
fixSteps:
In supabase/functions/cv-rewrite/index.ts, add an import alongside the existing auth import:
`import { pseudonymizeCv } from "../_shared/cv-pseudonymize.ts";`

Narrow the candidates SELECT at lines 30-35 to drop columns the gateway must never receive. Change the select list to remove `email, phone, address_city, date_of_birth, nationality` and keep only what the CV prose needs:
`.select("id, first_name, last_name, skills, languages, certifications, ai_summary, ai_target_functions, ai_function_group")`
(first_name/last_name are still selected so pseudonymizeCv can target them by name in any free text; they are NOT placed into the outbound payload — see next step.)

Replace the candidateInfo block (lines 67-78) entirely. Do NOT branch on `anonymous` for identity; always send a minimized, identifier-free professional object. The candidate's real name/contact are re-attached client-side (CvTool.tsx:130), so the prompt never needs them:
```
const candidateProfile = {
  reference: candidate.id?.substring(0, 6)?.toUpperCase() || "REF",
  skills: candidate.skills,
  languages: candidate.languages,
  certifications: candidate.certifications,
  ai_summary: candidate.ai_summary,
  ai_target_functions: candidate.ai_target_functions,
  ai_function_group: candidate.ai_function_group,
};
```

Simplify the systemPrompt (lines 80-83): since the payload is now always identifier-free, the `anonymous` conditional sentence is no longer about hiding identity but only about output style. Keep the anonymous-output instruction but base it on `anonymous` only for the rendered output preference; the data sent is minimized regardless. Concretely, leave systemPrompt as-is functionally but the `${anonymous ? ...}` clause now only affects wording of the generated text, which is harmless. (Optional: keep `anonymous` destructured at line 17 for this output-style toggle.)
Verify no remaining reference to `candidateInfo` exists (it is fully replaced by `candidateProfile` + pseudonymized `userPrompt`). Run deno check + typecheck (see verifyCmd).
verifyCmd: deno check supabase/functions/cv-rewrite/index.ts && npm run typecheck
risk: Low. The change only restricts what is sent to the external gateway; CV section prose quality is unaffected because identifiers/DOB/nationality were never used to generate professional sections (name is rendered client-side, CvTool.tsx:130). Possible minor behavior change: the AI no longer sees DOB/nationality/contact, so it cannot accidentally echo them — which is the intended outcome. De-risk by (1) keeping `ai_summary`/skills/languages/certifications so the prose stays rich, (2) running pseudonymizeCv as a net so any free-text leakage in those fields is also stripped, (3) confirming via `deno check` that `candidateInfo` has no dangling references. No DB or RLS change, so no tenant-isolation risk. Deploy via Supabase MCP deploy_edge_function after merge (standard edge-function deploy, no prod data touched).

title: No right-to-erasure / anonymize path (AVG art.17); candidate FKs block hard delete; no retention cron
evidence:
CONFIRMED — three sub-claims all hold in this code/DB.

(1) No erasure/anonymize implementation exists. `grep -rl "anonymize|anonymise|erase_candidate|delete_candidate|recht-op-verwijdering" supabase/ src/` returns nothing. No RPC, no edge function, no migration. The only candidate-facing destructive RPC is `merge_candidate_records` (supabase/migrations/20260604120000_dedup_candidates.sql:6-206) which deletes a *loser* duplicate but is not an AVG-erasure path (it repoints data to a survivor, it does not anonymize/forget a person).

(2) "FKs block delete" — verified against the LIVE DB (project noaupcteygfvlyymqtew). 24 child tables reference candidates with ON DELETE NO ACTION (annual_statements, contracts, payslips, placements, timesheets, sick_reports, housing_assignments, invoice_lines, hour_letters, mileage_entries, fuel_card_transactions, key_registrations, regulation_acknowledgements, onboarding_responses, onboarding_tokens, portal_invites, vehicle_assignments, vehicle_damage_reports, vehicle_fines, employee_deductions, employee_notifications, employee_reservations, employee_subsidies, candidate_profile_tokens) and 3 with ON DELETE RESTRICT (documents, employees, matches). Any one existing child row makes `DELETE FROM candidates` raise a foreign_key_violation. Source: live pg_constraint query (confdeltype) + migration text supabase/migrations/20260402130000_merge_candidates_employees.sql:114-204 (these ALTER TABLE ... REFERENCES public.candidates(id) lines have no ON DELETE clause → default NO ACTION). Only 13 tables CASCADE and 3 SET NULL.

(3) No retention cron. `grep -rln "cron.schedule" supabase/migrations/` lists 7 cron migrations (vehicle-apk, automated-messages, talentpools, housing-reminder, job-feed, loyalty); none does retention/anonymize. No `app.candidate_retention` or similar.

(4) No UI path. In src/components/candidates/* and src/pages/CandidateDetail.tsx there is no delete/erase action — the only `.delete()` in candidate components is talentpool membership (src/components/candidates/tabs/CandidateTalentpoolsTab.tsx:80). The action DropdownMenu (src/pages/CandidateDetail.tsx:273-289) currently only offers "Status wijzigen".

PII surface to erase (candidates Row, types.ts:826-900): first_name,last_name,middle_name,initials,email,phone,phone_nl,bsn,iban,bank_account_holder,date_of_birth,birth_place,birth_country,nationality,gender,marital_status,address_*,emergency_contact_name,emergency_contact_phone,id_document_number,id_document_type,id_document_valid_until,notes,availability_notes,cv_file_url,cv_raw_text,ai_analysis,ai_summary,external_id,employee_number,plus free-text in public.notes (polymorphic, related_entity_type='candidate') and storage objects via documents.file_path (documents.candidate_id is NOT NULL, ON DELETE RESTRICT).
rootCause: The schema was built additively (merge of candidates+employees in 20260402130000) without ever defining a data-subject lifecycle: child FKs default to NO ACTION/RESTRICT so a person can never be hard-deleted once they have any placement/timesheet/document/match, and no anonymize-in-place primitive was ever written. AVG art.17 (right to erasure) and art.5(1)(e) (storage limitation/retention) therefore have no technical implementation. Hard delete is also the wrong tool here: financial/fiscal records (invoice_lines, payslips, annual_statements, timesheets) carry a 7-year statutory retention obligation (Belastingdienst), so the correct primitive is anonymize-in-place (scrub direct identifiers, keep financial rows referentially intact) rather than DELETE.
fixSummary: Add an anonymize-in-place erasure primitive: a SECURITY DEFINER RPC `anonymize_candidate(p_candidate_id, p_reason)` that scrubs all direct identifiers on the candidate row, deletes CASCADE-safe PII-bearing children (documents rows after the edge function removes their storage objects, communications bodies, notes, cv/ai fields), keeps financial/fiscal rows (invoice_lines, payslips, annual_statements, timesheets) intact (they only reference candidate_id, no PII duplicated), marks the candidate `status='uitgeschreven'` + a new `anonymized_at` column, and writes an audit_log entry. Gate it with is_internal_user() (mirror existing pattern) and revoke from anon. An `erase-candidate` edge function (verify_jwt=false + self-auth requireInternalProfile) first deletes Storage objects (documents bucket) for the candidate, then calls the RPC via service role. Wire an admin-only "AVG: gegevens wissen" item into the existing CandidateDetail action menu behind an AlertDialog with typed confirmation. Add an opt-in retention cron migration (commented, like housing-reminder) that anonymizes candidates uitgeschreven > N years. NOT destructive-to-financials by design; destructive to PII (intended).
fixSteps: 1. Migration 20260615120000_candidate_erasure_avg17.sql — add column: `ALTER TABLE public.candidates ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS anonymized_at timestamptz;` and an index-free marker.

3. Create edge function supabase/functions/erase-candidate/index.ts (verify_jwt=false). Pattern: read Authorization header, `requireInternalProfile` from _shared/auth.ts (mirror data-export/index.ts usage), resolve candidate org-scope, list documents.file_path for the candidate, `supabase.storage.from('documents').remove([...paths])`, then `supabase.rpc('anonymize_candidate',{p_candidate_id, p_reason})` with the service-role client. Return JSON result. This ensures Storage PII (CVs, ID scans) is actually erased, not just the DB pointer.
4. Register the function in supabase/config.toml mirroring an existing protected self-auth entry: `[functions.erase-candidate]` with `verify_jwt = false`.

5. UI: in src/pages/CandidateDetail.tsx import `useAuth` (mirror src/pages/Companies.tsx:17,25 → `const { role } = useAuth();`). Add a new admin-only DropdownMenuItem inside the existing menu (after the Status wijzigen sub, lines 287-288): `{role === 'admin' && <DropdownMenuItem className='text-destructive' onClick={() => setEraseOpen(true)}>AVG: gegevens wissen</DropdownMenuItem>}`. Add a confirmation AlertDialog (AlertDialog is already imported, line 8) requiring the user to type the candidate's name or the word WISSEN, plus an erase useMutation that calls `supabase.functions.invoke('erase-candidate',{body:{candidate_id:id, reason}})`, then `qc.invalidateQueries(['candidate', id])`, `qc.invalidateQueries(['candidates'])`, toast.success and navigate('/kandidaten'). Mirror the existing changeStatus mutation shape.

6. Regenerate types: `mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__generate_typescript_types` → write to src/integrations/supabase/types.ts so candidates.Row gains `anonymized_at` and Functions gains `anonymize_candidate` (avoids the `(supabase as any).rpc` cast, though the UI uses functions.invoke so a cast is acceptable interim).

7. Optional retention cron — add a SEPARATE commented migration (do NOT auto-schedule) mirroring supabase/migrations/20260430080000_housing_reminder_cron.sql, that on a daily schedule calls an `erase-candidate?mode=cron` (or a dedicated retention edge fn) to anonymize candidates with status='uitgeschreven' and updated_at older than the org retention window. Keep it opt-in (requires app.cron_secret) exactly like the housing cron, because retention period is a legal/business decision JA Werkt must set.
migrationSql:
-- AVG art.17 right-to-erasure: anonymize-in-place primitive for candidates.
-- Hard delete is impossible (24 NO ACTION + 3 RESTRICT child FKs) AND undesirable
-- (financial rows: invoice_lines/payslips/annual_statements/timesheets carry a
-- 7-year statutory retention). So we scrub direct identifiers and keep financial
-- rows referentially intact. Mirrors is_internal_user() gating + audit_log pattern.
--
-- NB before applying on prod: verify communications PII column names via list_tables
-- and confirm no additional PII-bearing CASCADE child exists; adjust the body to match.

BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE public.candidates
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS anonymized_at timestamptz;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.anonymize_candidate(p_candidate_id uuid, p_reason text DEFAULT NULL)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = 'public'
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_cand public.candidates%rowtype;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO v_cand FROM public.candidates WHERE id = p_candidate_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'anonymize_candidate: candidate % not found', p_candidate_id;
  END IF;

  -- Defense in depth: tenant + internal-role guard (runs as definer, RLS bypassed).
  IF v_cand.organization_id <> public.get_user_org_id() OR NOT public.is_internal_user() THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'anonymize_candidate: not permitted for this user';
  END IF;

  IF v_cand.anonymized_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('candidate', p_candidate_id, 'already_anonymized', true);
  END IF;

  -- Delete PII-bearing children that are NOT statutory financial records.
  -- (Storage objects behind documents.file_path are removed by the edge function first.)
  DELETE FROM public.documents              WHERE candidate_id = p_candidate_id;
  DELETE FROM public.onboarding_responses   WHERE candidate_id = p_candidate_id;
  DELETE FROM public.candidate_profile_tokens WHERE candidate_id = p_candidate_id;
  DELETE FROM public.notes
    WHERE related_entity_type = 'candidate' AND related_entity_id = p_candidate_id;

  -- Scrub free-text message bodies (keep rows for delivery/audit history, drop content).
  -- VERIFY these column names against the live communications schema before applying.
  UPDATE public.communications
     SET subject = NULL, body = NULL
   WHERE candidate_id = p_candidate_id;

  -- Scrub the candidate row itself (all direct identifiers + CV/AI derived data).
  UPDATE public.candidates SET
    first_name = '[gewist]', last_name = '[gewist]', middle_name = NULL, initials = NULL,
    email = NULL, phone = NULL, phone_nl = NULL,
    bsn = NULL, iban = NULL, bank_account_holder = NULL,
    date_of_birth = NULL, birth_place = NULL, birth_country = NULL,
    nationality = NULL, gender = NULL, marital_status = NULL,
    address_street = NULL, address_postal = NULL, address_city = NULL, address_country = NULL,
    address_lat = NULL, address_lng = NULL,
    emergency_contact_name = NULL, emergency_contact_phone = NULL,
    id_document_number = NULL, id_document_type = NULL, id_document_valid_until = NULL,
    notes = NULL, availability_notes = NULL, external_id = NULL,
    cv_file_url = NULL, cv_raw_text = NULL, cv_has_photo = NULL,
    cv_pseudonymization_meta = NULL, cv_pseudonymized_at = NULL,
    ai_analysis = NULL, ai_summary = NULL, ai_red_flags = NULL, ai_positive_signals = NULL,
    ai_risk_factors = NULL, ai_interview_questions = NULL, ai_target_functions = NULL,
    ai_languages = NULL, ai_classification = NULL, ai_function_group = NULL,
    ai_reliability_score = NULL, ai_status = NULL, ai_stability = NULL,
    status = 'uitgeschreven', portal_enabled = false, auth_user_id = NULL,
    anonymized_at = now()
  WHERE id = p_candidate_id;

  INSERT INTO public.audit_log
    (organization_id, user_id, action, table_name, record_id, old_values, new_values, reason)
  VALUES
    (v_cand.organization_id, auth.uid(), 'delete', 'candidates', p_candidate_id,
     to_jsonb(v_cand) - 'bsn' - 'iban',
     jsonb_build_object('anonymized', true),
     COALESCE(p_reason, 'AVG art.17 right-to-erasure'));

  RETURN jsonb_build_object('candidate', p_candidate_id, 'anonymized', true);
END;
$$;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.anonymize_candidate(uuid, text) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
GRANT  EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.anonymize_candidate(uuid, text) TO authenticated, service_role;

COMMIT;

newFiles.purpose: verify_jwt=false + self-auth (requireInternalProfile) edge function: removes the candidate's Storage objects (documents bucket) via service role, then calls anonymize_candidate RPC. Ensures Storage PII (CV/ID scans) is truly erased, not just the DB pointer. Mirrors data-export/index.ts auth pattern.

title: send-portal-invite returns single-use account-takeover token with no authorization (cross-tenant)
evidence: supabase/functions/send-portal-invite/index.ts only checks that *some* user exists, never role or org. Line 85-86: `const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser(); if (!user) return json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);` — any authenticated user (incl. role `medewerker`, or a user from a DIFFERENT org) passes. Lines 97-105: the invite is fetched with the SERVICE-ROLE client (`service`, created line 88-91) keyed ONLY on `.eq("id", invite_id)` with NO `organization_id` filter, so RLS is bypassed and there is zero tenant isolation. Lines 116-120 build the activation URL containing the secret token, line 135 and line 150 return `activation_url` (with the token) in the JSON response, and lines 125-132 email it. The token is a single-use account-activation secret: portal-activate/index.ts validates it (`.eq("token", token).is("used_at", null).gt("expires_at", ...)`, lines 33-36) then calls `supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.createUser({ email: invite.email, password, email_confirm: true })` (lines 69-74) and inserts a `profiles` row with role `medewerker` (lines 90-98) — i.e. whoever holds the token sets the password and owns the portal account. config.toml line 124-125 confirms `verify_jwt = false`, so all authorization must happen in-body and currently does not. Contrast the canonical sibling send-match-proposal/index.ts (lines 158-161, 179-180) which gates with `requireInternalProfile` then scopes the resource query with `.eq("id", match_id).eq("organization_id", orgId)`. The auth helper already exposes exactly the needed primitive: _shared/auth.ts line 93-103 `requireInternalProfile` (rejects non-internal roles with 403) and returns `organizationId`.
rootCause: The function performs authentication (a valid session exists) but not authorization: it omits the internal-role gate and, critically, omits the `organization_id` scoping on the service-role invite lookup. Because the invite is read with the service-role client (RLS bypassed) and the secret activation token is returned in the response/email, any authenticated user — including a low-privilege `medewerker` or a user belonging to a different tenant — who supplies a valid `invite_id` can harvest another tenant's single-use activation token, enabling cross-tenant portal account takeover. This is the same class as audit item H1 in docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md.
fixSummary: Replace the bare `getUser()` check in send-portal-invite with the existing `requireInternalProfile` gate (internal roles only), and add `.eq("organization_id", auth.organizationId)` to the service-role invite lookup so an internal user can only resolve/send invites belonging to their own organization. No DB migration needed; the authorization helper and org-scoping pattern already exist and are mirrored from send-match-proposal. Response shape is unchanged (callers still receive `sent`, `to`, `activation_url`).
fixSteps: In supabase/functions/send-portal-invite/index.ts, add to the imports (top of file, after the existing imports on lines 1-3): `import { requireInternalProfile } from "../_shared/auth.ts";`

Scope the invite lookup to the caller's org: in the `.from("portal_invites")...` query (current lines 97-105) add `.eq("organization_id", orgId)` alongside `.eq("id", invite_id)` before `.maybeSingle()`. This guarantees an internal user from org A cannot resolve an invite_id belonging to org B (the lookup returns null → existing `if (!invite) return json({ error: "Invite not found" }, 404)` on line 107 handles it, avoiding info leak).
Replace the two remaining references to `user.id` (line 131 `sentBy: user.id` and line 147 `sent_by: user.id`) with `userId` from the auth object, since the local `user` variable no longer exists.

Leave the response bodies unchanged (lines 135 and 150 still return `activation_url`) — `src/pages/CandidateNew.tsx:231` consumes it and the caller is now guaranteed to be an authorized same-org internal user. No frontend change required: both callers (src/components/vacancies/PlacementSheet.tsx:244, src/pages/CandidateNew.tsx:222) already invoke from authenticated internal sessions and pass only `{ invite_id }`.
risk: Risk: if any legitimate caller invoked this function with a service-role token or as a non-internal role, the new gate would now 401/403 it. Verified there is no such caller — the only two invokers (src/components/vacancies/PlacementSheet.tsx:244 and src/pages/CandidateNew.tsx:222) run inside AuthProvider-wrapped internal-app screens (intercedent/admin/backoffice create placements and candidates) and pass only `{ invite_id }`; no cron/service-role path exists for this function. De-risk: after deploy, smoke-test the placement flow (PlacementSheet → 'Welkomstmail verstuurd' toast) and the CandidateNew portal-invite flow (activation_url still rendered) once as an intercedent. The fix is purely additive authorization (deny-more), so the only failure mode is over-blocking, which is caught by that single smoke test. Edge function deploy is prod-touching (mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__deploy_edge_function), hence human go required; no DB/data change, fully reversible by redeploying the previous build.

title: voys-api anonymous SSRF/open-proxy + Voys token exfiltration (H2)
evidence:
CONFIRMED in this code. supabase/functions/voys-api/index.ts:
- Lines 10-15: `Deno.serve` reads `body.{endpoint, method, payload, api_token}` and only requires `endpoint` to be present. No auth gate before the token branch.
- Lines 11,17,20: `const { ... api_token: directToken } = body; let apiToken = directToken; if (!apiToken) { ...auth... }`. When the caller supplies `api_token` in the body, the entire auth block (lines 20-61) is SKIPPED. config.toml:188-189 sets `verify_jwt = false` for voys-api, so the function is reachable by any caller holding the public anon key (embedded in the frontend). Result: anyone can POST `{endpoint, api_token}` and have the edge function proxy a request with an attacker-supplied bearer token.
- SSRF / open-proxy: supabase/functions/_shared/voys-helpers.ts:27-40 `getVoysBaseUrl` line 28 `if (endpoint.startsWith(\"http\")) return \"\";` and lines 52-53 in `callVoysApi` `if (endpoint.startsWith(\"http\")) { fullUrl = endpoint; }` — a caller-supplied `endpoint` starting with `http` is fetched VERBATIM (line 68 `fetch(fullUrl, ...)`). No allowlist of Voys hosts. Combined with the directToken bypass + verify_jwt=false, an unauthenticated caller can make the function fetch ANY arbitrary URL (full SSRF / blind open-proxy).
- Token exfiltration: helpers.ts:60-63 always attaches `Authorization: Bearer ${apiToken}` to `fullUrl`. Because `fullUrl` can be any http(s) URL (lines 52-53), the bearer is forwarded to an attacker-controlled host — i.e. any token reaching this code can be exfiltrated to an external host the attacker picks.
Contrast: sibling supabase/functions/voys-sync-calls/index.ts:9-33 has NO directToken bypass — it always authenticates. Repo already has hardened helper supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts:93-103 `requireInternalProfile` (used by cv-rewrite/index.ts:13, match-bulk-notify, send-match-proposal) and a SQL `is_internal_user()` gate (migrations 20260514121000, 20260507093000). voys-api uses none of these. Issue is REAL and unmitigated on launch-ready-fixes.
rootCause: Two compounding flaws: (1) voys-api accepts a caller-supplied `api_token` (directToken) in the request body which short-circuits all authentication, so with verify_jwt=false the function is an unauthenticated proxy. (2) `callVoysApi`/`getVoysBaseUrl` in voys-helpers.ts treat any `endpoint` beginning with `http` as a full fetchable URL with no host allowlist, turning the proxy into a full SSRF/open-proxy that also forwards the bearer token to attacker-chosen hosts. Together: anonymous SSRF + token relay/exfiltration. The only legitimate need for a caller-supplied token is the one-time validate-before-save step in the connect wizard (VoysSettings.tsx:37-60), which must still be authenticated and endpoint-restricted.
fixSummary: Gate voys-api behind requireInternalProfile (authenticated internal-role user only), remove the unauthenticated directToken proxy path, and harden voys-helpers.ts to reject any caller-supplied absolute URL (force endpoints onto the fixed Voys host allowlist). Keep the connect-wizard validate-token flow working by allowing an authenticated internal user to pass a candidate token ONLY for a hardcoded validation-endpoint allowlist, with the URL still built from the allowlisted base (never from caller input).
fixSteps: supabase/functions/_shared/voys-helpers.ts — close the SSRF hole. Remove the absolute-URL acceptance: delete `if (endpoint.startsWith("http")) { fullUrl = endpoint; }` (callVoysApi lines 52-54) and `if (endpoint.startsWith("http")) return "";` (getVoysBaseUrl line 28). In callVoysApi, normalize+reject untrusted input: `const clean = String(endpoint).replace(/^\/+/, ""); if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(endpoint) || clean.includes("..")) throw new Error("invalid endpoint");`. Always build `fullUrl = `${getVoysBaseUrl(clean)}/${clean}`` from the three fixed bases. Then defensively pin the host: `const allowedHosts = new Set(["api.voys.nl", "api.eu-production.holodeck.voys.nl"]); if (!allowedHosts.has(new URL(fullUrl).hostname)) throw new Error("host not allowed");`. This makes SSRF impossible regardless of auth state.

supabase/functions/voys-api/index.ts — require authentication for ALL calls. Add `import { requireInternalProfile, createAdminClient } from "../_shared/auth.ts";`. After the OPTIONS check, inside try: `const auth = await requireInternalProfile(req, corsHeaders); if (auth instanceof Response) return auth;`. Resolve the org token from `auth.organizationId` via the existing `get_voys_token` RPC using a service client (mirror voys-sync-calls/index.ts:38-52). DO NOT trust a body token for normal calls.

supabase/functions/voys-api/index.ts — handle the connect-wizard validation case safely. The wizard (VoysSettings.tsx:37-60) validates an unsaved token. Accept body `api_token` ONLY when the request is already authenticated as internal (guaranteed by step 2) AND `endpoint` is on a validation allowlist: `const VALIDATE_ENDPOINTS = new Set(["users/auth-context"]); const validateUserDetails = /^user\/[0-9a-f-]{36}\/details\/?$/i.test(endpoint); const isValidate = typeof directToken === "string" && directToken.length > 0 && (VALIDATE_ENDPOINTS.has(endpoint) || validateUserDetails);`. If isValidate, use directToken as apiToken but still route through the hardened callVoysApi (step 1) so the host stays pinned to Voys. If directToken is supplied but endpoint is NOT on the allowlist, return jsonError('endpoint not allowed for token validation', 400) — prevents using the wizard path as a general open-proxy. Otherwise ignore body api_token and use the org token.

supabase/functions/voys-api/index.ts — CORS consistency: pass `corsHeaders` (from voys-helpers) to `requireInternalProfile`. Keep `callVoysApi(apiToken, endpoint, method, payload)` call shape unchanged (index.ts:68); hardening is internal to the helper.

src/components/settings/VoysSettings.tsx — no functional change required IF the validation allowlist (step 3) covers `users/auth-context` and the `user/<uuid>/details/` regex. The component already invokes voys-api with the user JWT, so requireInternalProfile passes for admin/intercedent/backoffice/finance. The DB-write lines (69/83) are direct table writes, not voys-api calls — leave unchanged. If connect must be admin-only, tighten the validate branch to `auth.role === 'admin'`.

Deploy voys-api via mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__deploy_edge_function; keep verify_jwt=false (auth enforced in-body per project convention). Optionally apply the get_voys_token anon-REVOKE migration (migrationSql) as belt-and-braces.
migrationSql:
-- Belt-and-braces hardening for B5 (H2): ensure the Voys token-decryption RPC
-- can never be invoked anonymously. voys-api now authenticates in-body, but
-- get_voys_token is SECURITY DEFINER and returns the PLAINTEXT token, so it must
-- not be exposed to anon/PUBLIC. Mirrors 20260507093000_security_advisor_execute_grants_followup.sql.
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_voys_token(uuid) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_voys_token(uuid) TO service_role;
-- (authenticated does not need direct execute: the edge function uses service_role)
verifyCmd: deno check supabase/functions/voys-api/index.ts supabase/functions/_shared/voys-helpers.ts && npm run typecheck
risk: Functional risk: the connect wizard validates an unsaved token via two voys-api calls (users/auth-context and user/<uuid>/details/). If the validation allowlist is too narrow, connect breaks — mitigate by including both patterns in VALIDATE_ENDPOINTS before deploy and manually exercising the Voys connect flow. Behavioral risk: any caller relying on absolute http endpoints now gets 'invalid endpoint'; grep shows only VoysSettings.tsx calls voys-api and it uses relative endpoints, so blast radius is contained. The REVOKE migration is non-destructive (grants only) but prod-touching, so it needs a human go; voys-api decrypts a real org secret, so redeploy should be confirmed. De-risk: deploy the edge-function hardening first, smoke-test connect + sync, then apply the RPC REVOKE.

title: client_portal_invites RLS missing is_internal_user() -> opdrachtgever cross-company account takeover
evidence:
CONFIRMED. supabase/migrations/20260513183000_invite_tenant_policies_authenticated_only.sql:25-31 defines the only tenant policy on the table:
  DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_crud ON public.client_portal_invites;
  CREATE POLICY tenant_crud ON public.client_portal_invites FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (organization_id = get_user_org_id());
There is NO is_internal_user() gate and NO WITH CHECK clause (so for FOR ALL, INSERT inherits USING). An opdrachtgever user is a real authenticated principal: the activation edge function gives them a profiles row with organization_id = the agency org and role='opdrachtgever' (supabase/functions/client-portal-activate/index.ts:89-97). get_user_org_id() therefore returns the agency org for them, satisfying the only USING predicate.

The role-gating migration that added is_internal_user() everywhere EXPLICITLY skipped this table: supabase/migrations/20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql:677 -- "portal_invites / client_portal_invites — handled via edge function + will be fixed as part of PortalActivate rewrite." That follow-up never landed: grep shows only 3 migrations touch the table (portal_role_gating skip-note, 20260513183000 tenant_crud, 20260513193000 which only DROPs the old anon public_token_read) and none re-add is_internal_user(). No later migration overrides tenant_crud.

Table columns include the secret token (src/integrations/supabase/types.ts:1335-1346: token, email, company_contact_id, company_id, used_at, expires_at). The activation function trusts any unused/unexpired token row wholesale (client-portal-activate/index.ts:30-119): it creates an auth user for invite.email, inserts an opdrachtgever profile, and links company_contacts.auth_user_id — scoped to whatever company_contact_id the invite row names.

Exploit paths for any logged-in opdrachtgever:
1) SELECT * FROM client_portal_invites -> reads token/email for every OTHER client company's pending invite in the agency org -> open /klantportaal/activeren/{token} -> takeover of another company's portal (their placements/timesheets/candidates via the get_client_portal_company_id()-scoped policies in 20260513185000).
2) INSERT a forged row {organization_id: own org, company_contact_id: <victim company contact>, company_id: <victim company>, email: attacker@evil} -> self-activate -> escalate into any client company's portal.
The sibling portal_invites (employee) table has the identical defect at the same migration lines 3-23 (medewerker takeover), but B6 is scoped to client_portal_invites.
rootCause: The org-wide tenant_crud policy on public.client_portal_invites was written as FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (organization_id = get_user_org_id()) with no role gate. opdrachtgever (and medewerker) users share the same organization_id as internal staff in their profiles row, so get_user_org_id() returns the agency org for them and the policy grants full read/write over all invite rows (including the activation token). The portal_role_gating migration that added is_internal_user() to every other tenant table deliberately deferred the invite tables to a later edge-function rewrite that was never completed, leaving these two tables as the only non-internal-gated tenant policies. RLS is the only control because the public token-read policy was already removed and activation now flows through a service-role edge function — but that function fully trusts whatever invite row exists.
fixSummary: Add a new forward-only migration that replaces the over-broad org-only tenant_crud policy on public.client_portal_invites with internal-staff-only policies gated on public.is_internal_user(), mirroring the established 20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql pattern. Apply the identical hardening to the sibling public.portal_invites (employee) policies in the same migration since they share the exact same defect and the same root cause. Activation continues to work because it runs through the service-role client-portal-activate / portal-activate edge functions, which bypass RLS. No frontend change needed: the invite-creation UI (ClientPortalActivateSheet.tsx) runs as an internal admin/intercedent user, who passes is_internal_user().
fixSteps: Create supabase/migrations/20260615120000_invite_tables_internal_only_rls.sql with the SQL in migrationSql below. It DROPs the org-only policies and recreates internal-gated equivalents for both invite tables, mirroring the is_internal_user() pattern from 20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql.

For client_portal_invites: DROP POLICY tenant_crud and replace with a single FOR ALL policy: USING (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user()) WITH CHECK (same). This keeps internal SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE working for the invite-creation UI while blocking opdrachtgever entirely (no _self_ policy is needed for invites — opdrachtgever has zero legitimate need to read/write invite rows; activation is service-role-only).

For portal_invites (employee): DROP the three org-only policies (portal_invites_insert / portal_invites_select / portal_invites_update from 20260513183000 lines 3-23) and recreate each with the added AND public.is_internal_user() gate, keeping the same FOR/TO/USING/WITH CHECK shape.
Confirm no anon/public read policy remains on either table (20260513193000 already dropped public_token_read and portal_invites_public_token_read); the new migration does not re-add any.
Apply via Supabase MCP mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__apply_migration (or npx supabase db push) to project noaupcteygfvlyymqtew. THIS IS PROD-TOUCHING — requires human go.

After applying, run mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__get_advisors (type: security) to confirm no new RLS warnings, and smoke-test: (a) internal admin can still create an invite via the Opdrachtgeverportaal activeren sheet; (b) an opdrachtgever session returns 0 rows / permission denied on SELECT and INSERT against client_portal_invites; (c) /klantportaal/activeren/{token} still activates via the edge function.
migrationSql:
-- B6: client_portal_invites (and sibling portal_invites) tenant policies were
-- gated only on organization_id = get_user_org_id(), with NO is_internal_user()
-- check. opdrachtgever/medewerker users share the agency organization_id, so they
-- could SELECT every invite token in the org (cross-company account takeover) and
-- INSERT forged invites to self-escalate. Gate both tables to internal staff only,
-- mirroring 20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql. Activation runs via service-role
-- edge functions (client-portal-activate / portal-activate), which bypass RLS, so
-- token-based activation is unaffected.

BEGIN;

-- ----- client_portal_invites (opdrachtgever invites) -------------------------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_crud ON public.client_portal_invites;

CREATE POLICY tenant_crud
ON public.client_portal_invites
FOR ALL
TO authenticated
USING (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
)
WITH CHECK (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
);

-- ----- portal_invites (employee/medewerker invites) -- identical defect ------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS portal_invites_insert ON public.portal_invites;
CREATE POLICY portal_invites_insert
ON public.portal_invites
FOR INSERT
TO authenticated
WITH CHECK (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
);

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS portal_invites_select ON public.portal_invites;
CREATE POLICY portal_invites_select
ON public.portal_invites
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
);

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS portal_invites_update ON public.portal_invites;
CREATE POLICY portal_invites_update
ON public.portal_invites
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
)
WITH CHECK (
  organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()
  AND public.is_internal_user()
);

COMMIT;

newFiles.purpose: Replace org-only tenant policies on client_portal_invites and portal_invites with internal-staff-only (is_internal_user()) policies, closing the opdrachtgever/medewerker invite-token leak and forged-invite escalation.

verifyCmd: npx supabase db lint --file supabase/migrations/20260615120000_invite_tables_internal_only_rls.sql || true; then apply via Supabase MCP and run get_advisors(security)
risk: Risk: if any legitimate flow reads/writes these invite tables as a NON-internal role, it would break. Verified there is none: invite creation (src/components/companies/ClientPortalActivateSheet.tsx and the employee equivalent) runs as admin/intercedent (internal -> passes is_internal_user()); activation runs through service-role edge functions client-portal-activate/index.ts and portal-activate, which bypass RLS entirely; the public anon read policies were already dropped in 20260513193000. No tests reference client_portal_invites or tenant_crud (grep of tests/ and src/test/ is empty). De-risk: apply, then in an opdrachtgever session confirm SELECT/INSERT on client_portal_invites returns no rows / denied, and confirm an internal user can still create an invite and a token still activates. The migration is forward-only and non-destructive (policy swap only); rollback = recreate the old org-only policy if a regression appears.

title: vehicle_damage_reports org-wide {public} RLS policies let portal (medewerker) users read/modify/delete colleagues' damage reports
evidence:
Live DB (project noaupcteygfvlyymqtew) pg_policy dump for public.vehicle_damage_reports shows 6 PERMISSIVE policies, all applied to PUBLIC (polroles=[0], i.e. every role incl. authenticated/medewerker):
- vehicle_damage_reports_select_policy (SELECT): USING (organization_id = (SELECT profiles.organization_id FROM profiles WHERE profiles.id = auth.uid()))  -- NO role gate
- vehicle_damage_reports_update_policy (UPDATE): same org-wide USING+CHECK, no role gate
- vehicle_damage_reports_insert_policy (INSERT): WITH CHECK org-wide, no role gate
- vehicle_damage_reports_delete_policy (DELETE): USING org-wide, no role gate
- damage_self_select (SELECT) + damage_self_insert (INSERT): correctly scoped via employee_id IN (SELECT employees.id WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()) -- the legit portal path.
Because permissive policies are OR'd, a medewerker (portal) user whose profiles.organization_id is set matches the generic *_policy rules and can SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE EVERY damage report in the org. Confirmed material: 11 medewerker profiles have organization_id set; table holds 35 rows.
This is the exact gap that migration supabase/migrations/20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql closed for every other fleet table — it rewrote vehicles, vehicle_fines, vehicle_assignments, mileage_entries tenant_select/update to (organization_id = get_user_org_id()) AND is_internal_user() (verified live: candidates/vehicle_fines/mileage_entries/vehicle_assignments tenant_select all now carry is_internal_user()), but vehicle_damage_reports was never touched by it (grep: file does not mention vehicle_damage_reports). is_internal_user() exists in prod (SECURITY DEFINER). Portal own-data read continues to work via the existing damage_self_select policy (same employees.auth_user_id mechanism as vehicle_assignment_self_select / sick_self_select that the portal already relies on).
rootCause: vehicle_damage_reports predates the portal-role-gating sweep. Its baseline CRUD policies gate only on org membership (profiles.organization_id = auth.uid()'s org) with no role check, granted to PUBLIC. The 20260422130000_portal_role_gating migration that added is_internal_user() to all sibling tenant tables omitted vehicle_damage_reports (it was added/extended later by the 2026-05-13 damage-routing migration but that migration only added columns/constraints, never revisited RLS). Net: any authenticated user in the org — including role=medewerker portal users — passes the generic policies and gets org-wide read/write/delete on all colleagues' vehicle damage reports.
fixSummary: Add a new migration that rewrites the 4 generic vehicle_damage_reports_*_policy policies to require is_internal_user() (mirroring the already-deployed sibling fleet tables and the GROUP-C pattern in portal_role_gating), and switches the inline profiles subselect to the get_user_org_id() helper for consistency. Leave damage_self_select and damage_self_insert untouched so portal workers keep read/insert access to their OWN reports. No data change, no destructive op; pure policy redefinition. Apply via Supabase MCP apply_migration and keep the file in supabase/migrations/ for CI/local parity.
fixSteps: Create supabase/migrations/20260615120000_vehicle_damage_reports_internal_rls.sql with the SQL in migrationSql (DROP + CREATE each of the 4 generic policies, gated on get_user_org_id() AND is_internal_user()).

Do NOT alter damage_self_select / damage_self_insert — they provide the portal worker's own-report read+insert path (employee_id via employees.auth_user_id), identical mechanism to vehicle_assignment_self_select which the portal already depends on.
Apply to production via mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__apply_migration (project noaupcteygfvlyymqtew, name 20260615120000_vehicle_damage_reports_internal_rls) — prod-touching, needs human go.
Re-run the verifyCmd policy query to confirm all 4 generic policies now contain is_internal_user() and the two damage_self_* policies are unchanged.
Run mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__get_advisors (type: security) after apply to confirm no new RLS advisories.

title: Housing INSERT RLS policies missing is_internal_user() gate
evidence:
CONFIRMED — real and live in production.

1) Live policy state (pg_policies, project noaupcteygfvlyymqtew). The five housing tables have INSERT policies that gate ONLY on org, NOT on role:
- properties.tenant_insert: cmd=INSERT, roles={public}, with_check=(organization_id = get_user_org_id())
- units.tenant_insert: same
- housing_assignments.tenant_insert: same
- housing_inspections.tenant_insert: same
- key_registrations.tenant_insert: same
Contrast on the SAME tables: tenant_select / tenant_update both carry "AND is_internal_user()", and tenant_delete carries "AND get_user_role() = 'admin'". Only INSERT is ungated.

2) Migration evidence for WHY: supabase/migrations/20260422130000_portal_role_gating.sql lines 49-51 explicitly state "we keep INSERT unchanged ... medewerker users typically don't INSERT tenant-level data" and lines 356-390 only rewrite SELECT/UPDATE for properties/units/housing_inspections/key_registrations; lines 167-175 only rewrite SELECT/UPDATE for housing_assignments. INSERT is never touched for these tables in any migration in supabase/migrations/ (grep for "tenant_insert ON public.(properties|units|housing_assignments|...)" returns nothing; the policies originate from the pre-history Lovable schema).

3) Reachability: get_user_org_id() = "select organization_id from public.profiles where id = auth.uid()" — resolves for ANY role. profiles counts: medewerker=11 (all with org), opdrachtgever=4 (all with org). So a portal/client-portal user satisfies with_check=(organization_id = get_user_org_id()) and can INSERT into all five housing tables in their own org (e.g. create bogus properties/units, or self-assign a housing_assignments row — the overbooking trigger blocks capacity, not authorization).

4) Canonical pattern proven: 20 other public-schema INSERT policies (candidates, documents, placements, timesheets, contracts, sick_reports, property_owners, skills, ...) all use with_check=((organization_id = get_user_org_id()) AND is_internal_user()). The five housing tables are the only outliers. No portal/client _self_ INSERT policy exists on any of these tables, so gating INSERT to internal users breaks no legitimate portal write path (portal access is read-only via property_self_select / unit_self_select / housing_self_select).
rootCause: The portal_role_gating migration (20260422130000) deliberately rewrote only SELECT and UPDATE policies to require is_internal_user(), and DELETE was already admin-gated, but it left INSERT policies as the original Lovable org-only "tenant_insert" (roles={public}, with_check = organization_id = get_user_org_id()). Because get_user_org_id() resolves an organization_id for medewerker and opdrachtgever profiles too, those non-internal portal users pass the INSERT WITH CHECK and can create properties, units, housing_assignments, housing_inspections, and key_registrations within their own org. The fix is to add the AND is_internal_user() clause to these five INSERT policies, mirroring the 20+ other internal tables.
fixSummary: Add `AND public.is_internal_user()` to the INSERT WITH CHECK on properties, units, housing_assignments, housing_inspections, and key_registrations, mirroring the existing canonical internal-table pattern. Scope the policies to `TO authenticated` (consistent with the rewritten tenant_select/tenant_update on these same tables) instead of the legacy roles={public}. Done via one idempotent migration that DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert + CREATE POLICY for each table. No data change, no portal write path broken.
fixSteps: Create migration file supabase/migrations/20260615000000_b8_housing_insert_internal_gate.sql with the SQL in migrationSql below. It is idempotent (DROP POLICY IF EXISTS ... then CREATE) and wraps all five tables in a single BEGIN/COMMIT.

For each of the five tables (properties, units, housing_assignments, housing_inspections, key_registrations): DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.<table>; then CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.<table> FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK ((organization_id = public.get_user_org_id()) AND public.is_internal_user());

Apply to production via Supabase MCP: mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__apply_migration (name '20260615000000_b8_housing_insert_internal_gate', the SQL body). This is the source of truth; the file in supabase/migrations/ is the mirror for local/CI consistency.
After applying, re-run the verifyCmd query to confirm all five tenant_insert with_check values now contain is_internal_user() and roles={authenticated}.
Run mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__get_advisors (type security) to confirm no new RLS advisor regressions.

No frontend change needed: housing CRUD is performed by internal roles (admin/intercedent/backoffice) who satisfy is_internal_user(); the 3-step housing assignment wizard runs in the main app (/huisvesting), not the portal. Spot-check the housing assignment flow in the app post-apply to confirm internal users can still INSERT.
migrationSql:
-- ============================================================================
-- B8 — Gate housing INSERT policies on is_internal_user()
--
-- The portal_role_gating migration (20260422130000) rewrote SELECT/UPDATE on
-- properties / units / housing_assignments / housing_inspections /
-- key_registrations to require is_internal_user(), and DELETE was already
-- admin-gated, but it intentionally left INSERT as the legacy Lovable
-- org-only "tenant_insert" (roles=public, with_check = organization_id =
-- get_user_org_id()). Because get_user_org_id() resolves an org for
-- medewerker / opdrachtgever portal users too, those non-internal users can
-- INSERT housing rows in their own org.
--
-- This mirrors the canonical internal-table INSERT pattern already used by
-- candidates, documents, placements, timesheets, property_owners, etc.:
--   WITH CHECK ((organization_id = get_user_org_id()) AND is_internal_user())
-- and aligns the policy role to TO authenticated (matching the rewritten
-- tenant_select / tenant_update on these same tables).
--
-- Non-destructive: no data is altered. Idempotent.
-- ============================================================================

BEGIN;

-- ----- properties
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.properties;
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.properties
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user());

-- ----- units
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.units;
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.units
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user());

-- ----- housing_assignments
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.housing_assignments;
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.housing_assignments
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user());

-- ----- housing_inspections
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.housing_inspections;
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.housing_inspections
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user());

-- ----- key_registrations
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_insert ON public.key_registrations;
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON public.key_registrations
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (organization_id = public.get_user_org_id() AND public.is_internal_user());

COMMIT;

Migration is idempotent and transactional; rollback = restore the prior policies (FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (organization_id = get_user_org_id())). Prod confirm needed only because it is RLS DDL on live tables.
